title: "Lab 8 · Midterm debrief + project kickoff"

---

**No graded notebook this week** (the lab grade takes your best 12 of the 14
notebook labs, and this session is one of the two that don't produce one). The
90 minutes go to two things you will not want to skip.

## Part 1 · Midterm debrief (≈ 30 min)

We walk the exam problem by problem, same order as on the paper:

- For each question: the intended solution, the *most common* wrong answer from
  the actual scripts, and which lecture section repairs it. (The
  [sample exam](../exams/midterm-sample.qmd) solutions follow the same format if
  you want a preview of the style.)
- Grading transparency: how partial credit was assigned on the open questions.
- Regrade process: one week from the day grades post, written request, the whole
  script is re-marked (your score can move in either direction — this keeps
  requests honest).

Scores are typically posted to Moodle before this session; if grading runs long,
the debrief still happens from the solution set and scores follow within days.

## Part 2 · Project kickoff (≈ 60 min)

Teams were formed in Week 6; the **proposal is due Week 9 (Oct 22)** — one page:
task, dataset, method, evaluation plan, main risk. This session is a structured
working hour to get your team from "topic" to "defensible plan":

1. **Lightning statements (15 min).** Each team, 60 seconds, no slides: *what*
   you predict/build, on *which* data, and how you'll know it worked. Saying it
   aloud to the room is the fastest known detector of vague plans.
2. **The four proposal questions (25 min, teams work, staff circulate).** Write
   one crisp sentence each:
   - the task, and why a *graph* method should help;
   - the dataset — confirmed downloadable *today*, license checked, size stated;
   - the baseline you must beat — per the course rule, at least one *non-graph*
     baseline;
   - the main risk, plus your fallback.
3. **Risk exchange (15 min).** Teams pair up and attack each other's plans for
   five minutes per side: leakage in the split? dataset too big for Colab?
   evaluation that flatters memory over inference? Every attack that lands now
   is a week saved in November.
4. **Sign-off (5 min).** Each team leaves with its four sentences reviewed by a
   staff member — that reviewed draft *is* the skeleton of your Week-9 proposal.

Come with: your team decided (2–3 people — if you are still teamless, arrive
early and we fix that first), a laptop per team, and the
[topic list](../project/topics.qmd) open. The
[project page](../project/index.qmd) has the full rubric and milestone calendar.

**Also today:** [HW2](../homeworks/hw2.qmd) is released — due Thursday, Oct 29.
It covers Weeks 5–7, so everything in it is fresh from the exam you just took.
